items.description: After upgrade, a record seeded with tracking_code 'A12-B7-S001' has batch_number 'B7' and serial_number 'S001'
After upgrade, a record seeded with tracking_code 'L1-BATCH22-9' of a different width has batch_number 'BATCH22' and serial_number '9'
After upgrade, a conforming record's tracking_code is still present and identical to its seeded value
After downgrade to down_revision then upgrade head, the seeded rows' batch_number and serial_number are re-backfilled to the values derived before the downgrade
When the backfill step fails mid-migration, stock_records stays at the prior revision with no batch_number/serial_number columns and no partially backfilled rows (add + backfill in one transaction)
The integration test session fixture asserts the engine dialect is postgresql and its URL equals the paired-branch DATABASE_URL from the environment, failing fast otherwise
After upgrade, records with tracking_code 'X-1' or bare 'c' have NULL batch_number and NULL serial_number
After upgrade, records with four-segment 'A-B-C-D' or empty-segment 'A--C' codes have NULL batch_number and NULL serial_number
After upgrade, a record with a NULL tracking_code remains present with NULL batch_number and NULL serial_number
After upgrade, a nonconforming record's tracking_code is still present and identical to its seeded value
On the real branch DB, a direct INSERT into stock_records with batch_number NULL succeeds and information_schema shows batch_number is_nullable YES with no column default

After upgrade over a mix of conforming and nonconforming records seeded with per-run-unique SKUs, the count of the test's own seeded stock_records rows (filtered by those SKUs) equals the number seeded (delta, not whole-table total)
After upgrade, every record's sku, location and quantity equal the pre-upgrade snapshot
After upgrade, a record whose tracking_code leading segment differs from its location keeps its original location
After downgrade then upgrade, every row survives with unchanged sku, location, quantity and tracking_code
After the expand migration, inserting a second stock_records row for an existing (sku, location) is rejected by the UNIQUE constraint on the real branch DB
After the expand migration, inserting a stock_records row with quantity -1 (per-run-unique sku) on the paired branch is rejected by CHECK (quantity >= 0)
After upgrade, the count of the test's own seeded stock_records rows and each row's (sku, location, quantity, tracking_code) equal the pre-upgrade snapshot
After downgrade to the expand migration's down_revision then upgrade head, every seeded row is kept and the same batch_number/serial_number are re-derived
The integrity probe over N seeded nonconforming codes reports level 'warning' with nonconforming_count exactly N
The integrity probe counts NULL tracking_code records as nonconforming
The integrity probe does not count conforming three-segment records as nonconforming
The integrity probe run as python -m app.services.tracking_code_integrity against the branch DATABASE_URL emits the warning with the exact count
With N seeded nonconforming codes (delta over the test's own rows), the probe returns level 'warning'
With N seeded nonconforming codes (delta over the test's own rows), the probe returns nonconforming_count equal to N
The expand migration still completes when nonconforming tracking codes are present (the probe never fails the migration)
The integrity probe entrypoint reads its database URL from the DATABASE_URL environment variable rather than a hard-coded value
